genxml.title: VPro (Odyssey) "Buzz" texture state: environment,
genxml.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
genxml.doc: Texture state words of the Odyssey command stream: environment, mode, LOD, offset and target blocks, and the opcodes that carry them.

struct.name: CLASS
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc: Texture class (the "class" columns above): the component set the environment sees, a 3-bit value stored in the sampler word bits 25:23 (BUZZ_DECODE.h SAMPLER.activation, which that file leaves as an unexplained 3-bit value; this file gives its source). The library returns it from the index and the OpenGL internal format the application named, so the class cannot be derived from the index alone. Established as the values returned; the names are inferred from the formats that give each. The board's use of the field is unknown.

struct.name: ENV_W1
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
Values 0, 6 and 7 are never sent. GL_PHASE_SGIX is not an environment mode: it is a filter, and sets bit 17 of the sampler word (BUZZ_DECODE.h).
Words 1 and 2 are the environment colour, four unsigned 12-bit channels. The conversion from a float x is the same as for the border colour (section 3): 0 for x <= 0, otherwise trunc(x * 4096) clamped to 4095. established as the width and conversion. The channel order is inferred: the notes say the words are packed like the border colour (red high, green low in word 1; blue high, alpha low in word 2) and do not read the order out of the store separately. Bits 31:24 of each word: unknown (the setter's stores of the colour never name them). Mode add overwrites all four channels with 4095, so both words carry 0xffffff. established.

struct.name: ENV_W3
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc: Words 3 and 4 are always zero for OpenGL texturing: the initialiser stores zero in both and no texture setter writes either. established as what is sent. Their meaning is unknown. The image-transfer steps save and restore the whole block as a copy, so they cannot change it.

struct.name: FIRSTLEVEL
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
The write coverage of the level descriptor words (the bits the library writes in word 1 are the format index 25:20, size code 31:30, pitch 11:0 and, from two internal paths only, the offset code 28:26) is in BUZZ_DECODE.h and the offset code is in section 6. Word 1 bit 29 and bits 19:12 are established as never written by the three routines that store level words, and inferred never written by any library code. What the board does with them, or with a descriptor past entry 63, is unknown.
First level descriptor index (id 0x006, count 1): bits 5:0 name the first level descriptor the texture unit reads. Activation writes 0 (the base level's descriptor); the on-board mipmap builder writes 60 (TEX_SCRATCH_LEVEL) and restores the saved word. Bits 31:6 have no writer and stay 0. established.

struct.name: LEVEL3D_W2
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
3D textures. established: the library fills one level-table entry for a 3D target and does not change the filter, so a 3D texture whose application asked for a mipmap filter reaches the board with a mipmap filter code in the sampler word and a single level descriptor. The board is inferred to read level 0 plainly (nearest or linear) for 3D: the vendor's porting guide and a published patent both say 3D mipmapping is not implemented. Deriving further volume levels from slice spacing would go beyond what the library names.
Slice exponent (level descriptor word 2, 3D targets only). The notes establish that activation writes level word 2 bits 11:0 for a 3D target, as the base-2 ceiling of the slice tile count (0 for a count below 2). BUZZ_DECODE.h lists that word as unknown because its sender list there predates this finding; this file carries the field under its own word name so the two do not overlap. Board reading: inferred (the only reading under which a later sample finds what an upload wrote).

struct.name: MODE_W1
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
detail_level is the detail level as a positive count, min(-level, 15): the field is five bits wide but the library never sends more than 15. detail_modulate is 1 for the modulate detail function and 0 for add. Detail texture entries sit at the top of the level table (section 5).
Operands 1, 2 and 3 (S, T, R). established as widths and as the values written. max_clamp bits 16:0, whole texels: trunc(2^n * clamp), n the level size exponent less the base level (at least 0), clamp the per-axis maximum-clamp parameter (default 1.0). The default is therefore the whole level size, not size less one. The conversion truncates and the 17-bit mask wraps; it does not saturate. Bit 17 and bits 31:24 are kept from the previous word and never named by a store: unknown. wrap_aux bits 23:18, a 6-bit value set together with that axis's wrap mode in the sampler word (see WRAPAUX below). Its meaning on the board is unknown.

struct.name: MODE_W5
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
The R axis setter writes repeat to the sampler for any target but 3D (established). Any other wrap enumerant is refused by the library. The library sends every combination of the four modes on the three axes; a mixed state (for example S clamp, T repeat) reaches the board as the per-axis fields and nothing else. What the board does with a mixed state is unknown: every program the notes saw sets one wrap on all axes.
Operands 5 and 6: the border colour, four unsigned 12-bit channels, red in operand 5 bits 23:12, green in operand 5 bits 11:0, blue in operand 6 bits 23:12 and alpha in operand 6 bits 11:0. A float x converts as in section 2. established. Operand 5 bits 31:24 and operand 6 bits 31:25 are unknown. Operand 6 bit 24 is the offset flag (below). The default border colour the library writes: not recorded.

struct.name: OFFCODE
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc:
Code 3 is never sent (the allocator's table does accept element sizes of 16 and 32 bytes, codes 3 and 4, but no format row uses them).
Offset code (level descriptor word 1 bits 28:26, BUZZ_DECODE.h TEXLEVEL_W1.offset_code). Two writers: the on-board mipmap builder stores 2 only when the record's offset word equals 2, which the allocator never produces, so it stores 0; the pixel-to-texture move stores a value its helper derives from the source object's size and pixel-mode words: 0 for six of the pairs traced and 2 for exactly one pair; every other pair is a GL error. The builders traced give only pairs that map to 0, so code 2 is the move's only possible nonzero output and no traced path produces it: inferred unreachable in the shipped software, not excluded. Whether the board treats 1..7 differently from 0 is unknown.

struct.name: SIZE
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc: Size code c (level descriptor word 1 bits 31:30, BUZZ_DECODE.h TEXLEVEL_W1.size_code): 0 for indices 0..15 and 48, 1 for 16, 17, 18 and 49, 2 for 32 and 33. The allocator books 2 << c bytes per texel; the texture path and the pixel-to-texture move both send the same quantity (log2 bytes per texel minus 1), inferred for the move's every source object. Whether the board reads the field as a size, a layout selector or ignores it is unknown. The booked bytes are an upper bound for 2D textures (ICC levels book the full width while the pitch halves it) and a contract for 3D slices (section 5).

struct.name: TARGET
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc: Active texture target (id 0x005, count 1). The word is shared with the clip-plane and path-selection bits of the same block; only the target bits are listed. established as what the library sets: bit 5 for a complete 3D texture, else bit 4 for a complete 2D texture, else bit 3 for a complete 1D texture; bit 10 together with any of them. When no enabled target has a complete texture, bits 5:3 and 11:10 are cleared. Bit 11 is only ever cleared: unknown.

struct.name: WRAPAUX
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped GL library texture routines
struct.doc: Wrap modes are independent per axis: each setter takes one enumerant, writes one axis and looks at no other. The wrap codes themselves (0 repeat, 1 clamp to edge, 2 clamp, 3 clamp to border) are the sampler word's wrap_s, wrap_t and wrap_r fields (BUZZ_DECODE.h).
